# `Duration`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Duration — an opaque, unit-explicit time span.

A `Duration` replaces the bare millisecond `Int` that timeouts, delays,
intervals, retry backoff, and cache TTLs used to take.  The ONLY ways to
build one name their unit at the call site — `millis`, `seconds`,
`minutes` — so a number can never be silently misread as the wrong unit,
and the raw milliseconds a runtime kernel needs is recovered explicitly
with `toMillis`.

Every constructor clamps a negative input to zero: a duration is a
non-negative span, and a "minus-five-seconds timeout" is not a
representable value.  `zero` is the total identity span.

## `Duration`

An opaque, non-negative time span carried as whole milliseconds.  The
constructor is NOT exported, so a `Duration` is a proof of non-negativity.

## `millis`

```ipe
millis : Int -> Duration
```

`millis n` — a span of `n` milliseconds.  A negative `n` clamps to `0`.

## `seconds`

```ipe
seconds : Int -> Duration
```

`seconds n` — a span of `n` seconds.  A negative `n` clamps to `0`; an `n`
so large that `n * 1000` would overflow `Int` (i64) saturates to the largest
representable span rather than wrapping.

## `minutes`

```ipe
minutes : Int -> Duration
```

`minutes n` — a span of `n` minutes.  A negative `n` clamps to `0`; an `n`
so large that `n * 60000` would overflow `Int` (i64) saturates to the largest
representable span rather than wrapping.

## `zero`

```ipe
zero : Duration
```

The zero span (`0` ms).  A total value.

## `toMillis`

```ipe
toMillis : Duration -> Int
```

`toMillis d` — recover the whole-millisecond span for the runtime boundary.
